title: Valid 1D convolution
starter:
# y[i] = x[i]*w[0] + x[i+1]*w[1] + x[i+2]*w[2] for i in 0..3
# The starter only uses w[0]. Add a k loop that accumulates into y[i].
%x  = buffer 6 dtype=i32 slot=0
%w  = buffer 3 dtype=i32 slot=1
%y  = buffer 4 dtype=i32 slot=2
%i  = range 4
%xv = shrink %x %i shape=[]
%xe = load %xv
%wv = shrink %w 0 shape=[]
%we = load %wv
%p  = mul %xe %we
%yv = shrink %y %i shape=[]
%s  = store %yv %p
%ei = end %s %i
%y1 = after %y %ei

samples.label:
buffer slot 0 starts as [1 2 3 4 5 6]
buffer slot 1 starts as [1 0 -1]
final contents of slot 2

hints: Each output reads a window of 3 inputs starting at its own index: y[i] uses x[i], x[i+1], x[i+2].
Inside the `i` loop: store `0` at `y[i]`, take the version after that store, then run a `k` loop over 3 that loads `y[i]` from it, adds `x[i+k] * w[k]`, and stores back.
The offset `i + k` has interval [0, 3] + [0, 2] = [0, 5], which fits a 6-element `x` without any masking. Close the loops inner first: `end %s %k`, then `end ... %i`, then one top-level `after %y`.

answer.code:
%x  = buffer 6 dtype=i32 slot=0
%w  = buffer 3 dtype=i32 slot=1
%y  = buffer 4 dtype=i32 slot=2
%i  = range 4
%yv = shrink %y %i shape=[]
%z  = store %yv 0
%y0 = after %y %z
%k  = range 3
%ik = add %i %k
%xv = shrink %x %ik shape=[]
%xe = load %xv
%wv = shrink %w %k shape=[]
%we = load %wv
%p  = mul %xe %we
%yv0 = shrink %y0 %i shape=[]
%cur = load %yv0
%sum = add %cur %p
%s  = store %yv0 %sum
%ek = end %s %k
%ei = end %ek %i
%y1 = after %y %ei
answer.explain: A valid convolution never reads outside the input, so `i + k` is provably in [0, 5] straight from the range intervals. The accumulator is the output element itself, reset once per `i` by a store that depends on `i`, and the `k` loop's load sees the current sum on every iteration. The INT_MAX test checks that the sum wraps like i32 should.
